name: Hammurabi
description: Sixth king of the First Babylonian dynasty, who unified much of Mesopotamia and promulgated the Code of Hammurabi — one of the earliest surviving comprehensive legal codes, inscribed on a diorite stele with 282 laws governing commerce, property, family, and justice under the principle of proportional retribution.

name: Ramesses II
description: Third pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty, reigning 66 years. Fought the Hittites at Kadesh (c. 1274 BCE), concluding history's earliest surviving peace treaty, and built monumentally at Abu Simbel, Karnak, and the Ramesseum. His mummy survives in Cairo.
